title: Do you think a game made with AI-assisted coding but paid art and music would get the same hate as a fully AI-generated game?
author: Strafkai
selftext:
I've been wondering how people in the indie game dev community would react to a game built primarily through vibe coding, but with human-made art and music created by paid artists and composers.

Do you think it would still receive the same backlash as a game where the code, visuals, music, and other assets are all AI-generated?

I'm curious where people draw the line. Is the main issue the use of AI itself, the impact it has on developers and artists, or the perception that AI-generated games lack genuine human creativity?

If a developer uses AI to help build a game but still invests money in human artists, musicians, and other creatives, do you think that changes how the project should be perceived?

I'd love to hear what other developers think, especially those who are experimenting with AI tools in their workflows.
